description: New Municipal Planning Commission members received orientation.
Learned city planning and development processes.

segments.title: Municipal Planning Commission Overview
segments.takeaway: An overview of the Municipal Planning Commission's purpose, structure, reporting, meeting process, and member expectations was presented.

segments.title: Urban Land Development in Saskatoon Overview
segments.takeaway: Administration provided an overview of the Planning and Development Department's structure, the city's Official Community Plan, the typical development process, and upcoming major projects.

segments.title: Receive Information on Presentations
segments.takeaway: The committee moved to receive the information presented by administration regarding the Municipal Planning Commission and urban land development.

segments.title: Appointment of Chair and Vice Chair
segments.takeaway: Craig Carly was nominated and appointed as Chair for 2025, and the vote for Vice Chair was deferred to the end of the meeting.

segments.title: 2025 Membership Information
segments.takeaway: The committee received information regarding the appointments to the Municipal Planning Commission for the 2025 and 2027 terms.

segments.title: 2025 Meeting Dates Information
segments.takeaway: The committee received information regarding the Municipal Planning Commission's meeting dates for 2025.

segments.title: Confirmation of Agenda
segments.takeaway: The committee approved the agenda as presented.

segments.title: Declarations of Conflicts of Interest
segments.takeaway: No conflicts of interest were declared by the committee members.

segments.title: Adoption of Minutes
segments.takeaway: The minutes from the regular meeting of the MPC held on December 17th, 2024, were adopted.

segments.title: Secondary Suites in Semi-Detached Dwellings Amendments
segments.takeaway: Administration presented proposed amendments to allow secondary suites in semi-detached dwellings and to remove a redundant mechanical room access regulation from the zoning by-law.

segments.title: Repealing Direct Control District 2 Amendments
segments.takeaway: Administration presented proposed amendments to repeal Direct Control District 2 and re-designate lands to corridor mixed-use, station mixed-use, and corridor residential zoning districts.

description: Commission will appoint its Chair and Vice-Chair for 2025.
Rezones Idylwyld Drive, Stanley Place, Minto Place for higher density.
Allows multi-unit residential and mixed-use buildings.
Existing one-unit dwellings on Idylwyld Drive become non-conforming.

chips.text: Staff explained rezoning choice minimized non-conforming uses on narrow lots.
Residents on Minto, Aberdeen, Grey, Cannot cul-de-sacs own majority of properties.
Landowners expressed interest in development involving property consolidation.

description: Rezone 15 Eitherwild Drive sites to station mixed use.
Rezone 159 cul-de-sac sites to corridor residential.
Existing single-unit homes on Eitherwild Drive become non-conforming.

chips.text: Staff chose scenario two to minimize new non-conforming uses.
Residents on Minto, Aberdeen, Grey, and Knot own most properties.
Landowners expressed interest in development involving property consolidation.
Amendments remove local area plan's transition support for displaced residents.
Future zoning amendments could consider CM1 if sites are consolidated.

description: Updates city planning documents with new flood plain maps.
Removes a section on revoking development permits.
These changes are required for provincial bylaw approval.

chips.text: A councillor asked about development permits issued in error; staff confirmed it is rare.
Property owners in flood plains must consult the Water Security Agency for building elevation.
Section 4.3.6 was removed for consistency with the Planning and Development Act.
